content.text:
Repository /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork "JusPrin"). Work in your own new git worktree based on local branch `claude/no-save-prompts` (commits 7852470aff and d33fb306c9), or on origin/jusprin-newui once that branch contains them. Do not touch the main checkout or another session's worktree. Do not push.

Bug: the printer panel (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp, build_runtime) creates a fresh in-memory Agent::ProjectPersistence (storage.in_memory = true) every time it opens. The AgentHost takes tool action ids from that document (AgentHost.cpp: set_action_id_allocator -> ProjectStateDocument::allocate_action_id, which returns "t-1", "t-2", ...). Since 7852470aff the panel also installs the shell's version callbacks (host.tools().set_version_callbacks(version_before, version_after) in ShellController.cpp). version_after calls ProjectAutosave::record_agent_operation, which writes operations/<action_id>.json into the PROJECT's permanent version store. ProjectVersionStore::record_operation refuses an existing file ("operation version record already exists"). Result: the second versioned tool call (printer_change, or settings_apply_patch) from any later panel opening on the same project gets the same id "t-1". The change goes through, but the tool reports local_save_failed "The action ran, but its changes couldn't be saved. Check the project before trying again." The model then tells the person that a successful change failed. The panel's ids may also collide with the project agent pane's own "t-N" ids in the same store.

Reproduced 2026-10-14 with `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-setup`: after the existing check nozzle_panel_change_keeps_the_dropped_edit_in_history, a second call_in_panel(named, "printer_change", {nozzle 0.6}) on the same project changed the nozzle, dropped the unsaved printer_notes edit, and failed with that message; the log showed "Could not save after Agent action: operation version record already exists".

Fix: give the panel's action ids project-unique values. For example, take them from the shell's real project document, or add a per-opening unique prefix. Decide which and explain why. Add a shell harness check (tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp, printer-setup section near verify_nozzle_change_leaves_the_project) that makes two versioned panel calls in two openings on the same project and expects both to succeed. Show that the check fails before the fix. Build recipe: configure with /Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake, Ninja Multi-Config, --config Release, BUILD_TESTS=ON. Build targets jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs shell_integration_harness. Run the harness with an isolated HOME.

name: printer-panel-action-id-collision
description: "Printer panel restarts action ids at t-1 per opening but files versioned calls in the project's permanent history; the second opening's change succeeds yet reports local_save_failed (found 2026-10-14)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ef1c9e7b-9046-4021-b7fe-b659d08d3643
  modified: 2026-10-15T02:27:24.872Z
---

Found 2026-10-14 on `claude/no-save-prompts`. Ever since 7852470aff installed the shell's version callbacks on the printer panel, each panel opening has used a fresh in-memory ProjectPersistence, so its action ids restart at "t-1". ProjectVersionStore::record_operation then refuses the duplicate operations/t-1.json. A second versioned call (printer_change, settings_apply_patch) from a later opening on the same project goes through, but it reports local_save_failed "The action ran, but its changes couldn't be saved". A fix task chip was offered, but it was not fixed then.

**Why:** a false failure is the most likely thing a person sees after a panel change, and it looks like a save problem, not an id problem.

**How to apply:** when a panel tool reports local_save_failed with autosave state Saved, look for "operation version record already exists" in the log before blaming storage. Check whether this is fixed (grep PrinterPanel build_runtime for the id allocator) before trusting this note. The nozzle-change proposal is the untracked file nozzle-change-failed-proposal.md in worktree bold-cohen-1cf36c. Related: [[tool-call-approval-removed]], [[autosave-design-research]].

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: printer-live-harness-lessons
description: "--printer-live traps (2026-09-23): multi-line replies escape HARNESS-prefixed greps, failed runs keep a data dir holding the API key, and re-selecting a selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 54c192d0-38b5-4a46-8894-652694e43240
  modified: 2026-09-23T22:16:03.023Z
---

Lessons from driving the printer chat through `--printer-live` with the live model and the fake Bambu printer:

- **A reply's later lines have no `HARNESS LIVE` prefix.** A `Choices:` line sits on its own log line, so `grep "HARNESS LIVE"` hides it. On 2026-09-23 this produced a wrong report that the model never offered choices. Grep `^Choices:` separately.
- **A failed run keeps its data dir, with the API key in it.** The harness prints `HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: /var/folders/.../jusprin-shell-*`. Delete the dir your own run printed, by that path. Do not sweep every `jusprin-shell-*` holding a key: another session may be running the harness in the same checkout, and on 2026-09-23 a sweep deleted a live instance's data dir.
- **Re-selecting the selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it.** DevManager's "same lan machine" path disconnects and reconnects, and GUI_App's local-connect handler (CallAfter) then sees the lost status and calls `set_selected_machine("")` after the reconnect. The connection reports "The selected printer changed". `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` now deselects and re-selects on the next event turn. The fake printer auto-selects itself when discovered, so the first connect always hits this.
- **Close OrcaSlicer's printer list (GuideFrame) only after its page loads.** It installs its web page's script handler from a CallAfter that waits on the page; `EndModal` before the load leaves that wait hanging on a hidden view, and the app freezes with no window. On 2026-09-23 this was first blamed on the product and "fixed" with a deferral, then traced to the test and reverted. Wait for `!is_adding_script_handler()`, a non-busy page and a URL, as the old `setup_manual` check did.
- **Open the panel through `ShellController::open_printer_conversation`** in live tests; `PrinterPanel::open` skips the full-window layout.
- **The model's reliability is measured, not assumed.** gpt-5.4-mini saved changes without waiting for yes in 6 of 10 runs, even with an explicit "ask, then stop" prompt. Count across several runs before calling prompt wording fixed.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]].

name: workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac
description: "On macOS the workspace adapter harness never reaches GUI_App::post_init; closing its frame crashes, so it exits via ExitMainLoop unless post_initialized()"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ed4bbcf2-a467-44f4-bceb-b20f93cd25d8
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:28:53.409Z
---

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].

name: manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe
description: "Reproduce any JusPrin tool behaviour without a live model in about 20 s per run: shell harness --manual-mcp plus tests/mcp/probe.py call(); two traps (leaked harness from `cd && cmd &`, slice_start on an unchanged sliced plate)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 0b03c379-ea3d-491e-a0b3-9b5bf2a6240f
  modified: 2026-10-12T23:51:00.507Z
---

Used 2026-10-12 for the spiral vase investigation (branch `claude/spiral-vase-writable`).

**Recipe.** Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY` on stderr (about 15 s), read the URL from `<scratch dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`, then call tools with `probe.call(urlsplit(url), "tools/call", {"name": ..., "arguments": ...})` imported from `tests/mcp/probe.py`. The fixture is two plates, one 20 mm box each, Bambu X1C 0.4, "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C", "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", the same presets as Kenneth's live tests. Another session's harness can run at the same time; the port falls back from 47301 and the discovery file is per data dir.

**Trap 1: leaked harness.** In a script, `cd "$S" && nohup harness ... &` makes `$!` the subshell, so `kill $!` leaves the harness running, and the next run's `rm -rf <fixture>` fails with "Directory not empty". Write `cd "$S"; nohup harness ... &`. Check with `pgrep -fl "<worktree>.*JusPrinShellHarness"` before finishing.

**Trap 2: slice_start on a sliced, unchanged plate.** The fixture's plate 1 starts sliced. `slice_start` on it (with or without `wait`) left it reported `sliced: false`, `slice_report` `valid: false`, and with `wait: true` the probe saw the stream close with no reply. Orca's log says "background process in idle state, use previous result". Change a setting first, then slice. Not investigated further.

**Timings on this Mac, Release config, load 30 to 40:** fresh worktree build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests workspace_contract_tests setting_display_tests shell_integration_harness` was 905 steps in about 14 min; the shell harness default regression (549 checks) about 2 min; the workspace adapter harness (972 checks) under 1 min. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

**Seeding a preset (2026-10-12).** `--manual-mcp` does not wipe its directory at start, so a user preset written to `<fixture>/user/default/machine/<name>.json` before launch (keys `from: User`, `inherits`, `name`, `printer_settings_id`, `version`, plus the values under test) is loaded and can be named as a settings `target.preset`. A Python driver that starts the harness with `subprocess.Popen` and terminates it in `finally` avoids Trap 1.


**Why a plate will not slice (2026-10-15).** MCP `slice_report` on a plate Orca refuses says only `valid: false`, with no reason even with `sections: ["findings"]`, and `slice_start` still answers `started: true`. Orca's own refusal text is in `<fixture>/log/debug_*.log`: grep `validate err=`. Used to reproduce the PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate case (branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch`, worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12). See [[printer-setup-bed-type-check]].

**Slice waits, 2026-10-15 (jusprin-newui 336facf825).** Trap 2 re-measured: `slice_start {plateId, wait: true}` on the sliced, unchanged plate 1 got no reply in 120 s (a hang, follow-up task filed). Right after `printer_setup` fixes a plate Orca had refused, `slice_start` fails "That plate cannot be sliced as it stands" for about 3 s: the adapter checks `PartPlate::can_slice()`, whose invalid flag Orca refreshes only on its next deferred validation. A refused slice hanging the wait was fixed on branch `claude/slice-wait-refused` (worktree brave-panini-347b62): `WorkspaceSlicing::refused` carries Orca's ValidateError text. Over MCP every `unavailable_operation` reads as `workspace_unavailable` (McpProtocol.cpp), so don't take that code to mean JusPrin is closed.

content.text:
I fixed the bug and the new harness check shows it: before the fix, a printer change saved from a second printer-panel opening on the same project reported a false "couldn't be saved" error; after it, both changes save cleanly. The fix is in my own worktree (`.claude/worktrees/ecstatic-bun-665f72`, branch `claude/panel-action-ids`). It is not committed and not pushed.

**The base branch.** `claude/no-save-prompts` no longer contains 7852470aff and d33fb306c9 by those ids. On 2026-10-14 it was squashed into one commit, 336facf825, on top of `jusprin-newui` (6b4b8b6188). That squash contains both changes. The originals survive only on `backup/no-save-prompts-before-squash`. I based the work on 336facf825.

**Why I chose the project's own counter.** Each tool call gets an id like "t-3", and that id is the name of its record in the project's saved history. The panel now takes these ids from the project's own document, the same counter the project's agent pane uses. That gives one counter per history store. The counter is saved with the project, so it keeps counting up across panel openings and app restarts, and the panel can never repeat one of the agent pane's ids. A per-opening prefix would have worked too, but it would add a second id format, and its uniqueness would rest on a timestamp or random value instead of a counter. The panel's chat still lives in its own throwaway document; only the id comes from the project.

**The change (3 files):**
- [PrinterPanel.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.hpp): new `Callbacks::allocate_action_id`.
- [PrinterPanel.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp): `build_runtime` installs it with `set_action_id_allocator` next to the version callbacks. This applies only to the printer task; the filament chat saves nothing to the project's history, so it doesn't need it.
- [ShellController.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp): passes `m_persistence->document().allocate_action_id()`.

**Tests and results.** The new check, `verify_panel_changes_in_two_openings_are_both_saved` in [shell_harness.cpp](tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp), runs right after the existing nozzle check. It opens the panel twice on the same project and makes one `printer_change` in each. It expects both to succeed, the two ids to differ, and neither id to equal the next id the project's agent pane would get.
- **Before the fix:** `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-setup` with an isolated HOME gave `failures=4`, all four from the new check. Both openings got `t-1` and reported `local_save_failed`, and the log showed "Could not save after Agent action: operation version record already exists". Even the first opening failed, because the existing nozzle check had already written `operations/t-1.json`.
- **After the fix:** `--printer-setup` passes with 207 checks and no failures, and the default harness run passes with 553 checks and no failures.

**Remaining issue (not fixed).** If a project's agent document is unreadable, the app replaces it with a fresh one whose counters start at 1. The history folder still holds the old operation files, so both the agent pane and the panel would hit this same false error again. That predates this change; I only noticed it while reading the code.

I updated the memory note on this bug to record the fix. Say if you want me to commit the change on `claude/panel-action-ids`.
